messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on streaming/paging service (region: us-west-2). Current p95=320ms p99=2.1s. Error rate stable. Auto-mitigation not triggered.
jamal: saw it. digging into tail traces now — is this across all frontends or specific shard?
olivia: looks like elevated queueing on pager worker pool 7 (`pager-7`). p50/p90 OK, but p99 across streaming endpoints.
maria: linking recent deploys — we rolled a routing change 62m ago that toggled prefix salting for namespace hashing (build: routing-2026.03.14-09). could be correlated.
leo: confirmed: rollout toggled `prefix_salt_enabled=true` on canary two nodes -> gradually to 30%. that changes key distribution for the paging cache.
jamal: that would explain cache miss increase for aged prefixes. can someone post cache hit-rate around the spike window?
nana: (uploaded metric snippet) prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.92 -> 0.70 starting @3456788800; spillover into KV paging reads + websocket stall.
olivia: streaming logs show repeated cold loads and recompute of KV buckets, example traces: ```trace_id=tr-9f3a
span: pager.lookup -> kvcache.miss -> paging.read(12MB)
latency: 1800ms
```
maria: customer-impact: a handful of mid-market customers on dedicated capacity saw degraded response times for long-chat sessions (timeouts at 3s). CS alerted. tagging @customer-success.
customer-success: on it — collecting affected org ids, asking for list of sessions/times to scope SLA hit. sending preliminary notice to two accounts flagged by health probes.
jamal: mitigation plan: 1) pause prefix-salting rollout immediately, 2) increase prefetch concurrency on pager-7, 3) warm prefixes by replaying recent popular keys into cache, 4) failover a subset of traffic to legacy routing. thoughts?
leo: pausing rollout now: `kubectl set env deploy/routing SERVICE_PREFIX_SALT=false --namespace=platform` -> in progress.
olivia: increasing prefetch concurrency on pager-7: `svcctl scale pager --replicas +2 --annotation prefetch=high` — applied to us-west-2.
maria: starting cache-warm job: `./tools/prefetch --window=30m --top=50k --target=pager-7` (running as batch job). will monitor hit-rate delta.
jamal: also enabling temporary fallback to salted-compatible cache layer (read-through) to reduce tail reads. coordinating with eng-sre for rollback window.
leo: routing change paused at 3456789038. kubectl rollout paused and preserved revision routing-2026.03.14-08 as active.
nana: metrics update (2m after): prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.70 -> 0.81; p99 down from 2.1s -> 780ms. still above SLO (target p99 < 500ms).\olj: (typo) sorry — olivia continuing: live mitigation helped but some long tails persist on sessions with >10k token histories. likely KV read amplification.
maria: customer-success: staging notice sent. recommending a follow-up RCA + mitigation plan for dedicated customers. also draft communication for impacted customers with ETA for full remediation.
jamal: next steps: 1) finish warm-up job (15m), 2) run coordinated rollback of prefix-salt flag in remaining nodes, 3) create hotfix to reduce paged-read size (v0.9.1), 4) handoff to night oncall if not resolved in 45m. assign owners?
leo: I own rollback (in progress), olivia owns prefetch scaling + metric watch, maria owns customer comms, jamal owns RCA coordination and hotfix.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE at 3456789055: mitigation actions applied (rollout pause, prefetch up, cache-warm started). Estimated restore: partial; ongoing.
nana: warm-up job completed: heuristic warming covered ~72% of top prefixes. hit_rate now 0.88. p99 improved to 430ms across streaming endpoints.\jamal: excellent — p99 under SLO now. keeping this thread open for handoff notes and postmortem items.
customer-success: logged impacted orgs + compensation suggestion draft ready. will await final RCA.\maria: root cause hypothesis: prefix-salting deployment changed key distribution mid-roll; small hot sets lost locality -> cache churn -> paging amplification -> tail latency. probable contributing factor: TTLs on prefixes were short (600s) and warm-up pattern wasn't resilient to distribution flips.
jamal: action items for postmortem: - stop-rollout checklist (canary validation steps) - add rolling warm-up for prefix-salt toggles - increase default prefix TTL to 1800s behind feature flag - add canary synthetic for prefix-hit-rate before progressive rollout - build runbook for prefix-hash flips
leo: handing off to night oncall @ana at 3456789120. ana, please monitor p99, prefix_cache.hit_rate, and customer queue. escalation path: page jamal -> eng-sre.
nana: final note: no data loss, limited customer timeouts, elastic fallback prevented larger degradation. closing operations window unless regressions reappear. :white_check_mark:
